items.t: Rheumatoid arthritis (including juvenile), ankylosing spondylitis, osteoarthritis and other arthropathies; soft-tissue and periarticular conditions (e.g. frozen shoulder, bursitis, tendonitis, low back pain, sprains); mild to moderate pain such as dysmenorrhoea, dental and post-operative pain, headache and migraine.

src.q: Brufen is indicated for its analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis (including juvenile rheumatoid arthritis or Still's disease), ankylosing spondylitis, osteoarthritis

Brufen is also indicated for its analgesic effect in the relief of mild to moderate pain such as dysmenorrhoea, dental and post-operative pain and for the symptomatic relief of headache including migraine headache.

items.t: Suspension: mild to moderate pain, post-immunisation pyrexia, fever and cold/flu symptoms; on prescription also rheumatic and inflammatory conditions including juvenile rheumatoid arthritis.

src.q: is used as an analgesic for relief of mild to moderate muscular pain, post-immunisation pyrexia
rheumatoid arthritis (including juvenile rheumatoid arthritis or Still's disease)

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the SmPCs or the MHRA pages accessed (suspension SmPC splits indications into OTC and prescription-only).

items.t: Adults and children over 12 (tablets): 1200-1800 mg daily in divided doses; some patients can be maintained on 600-1200 mg daily. In severe or acute conditions may increase, but total must not exceed 2400 mg/day in divided doses. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time.

src.q: The recommended dosage of Brufen is 1200-1800 mg daily in divided doses. Some patients can be maintained on 600-1200 mg daily.
provided that the total daily dose does not exceed 2400 mg in divided doses

items.t: Suspension, adults and children over 12: 200-400 mg (10-20 ml) up to three times a day; at least 4 hours apart; maximum 1200 mg (60 ml) in 24 hours. See a doctor if needed for more than 10 days.

src.q: The recommended dose is 200 mg-400 mg (10-20 ml), up to three times a day as required. Leave at least four hours between doses and do not take more than 1200 mg (60 ml) in any 24 hour period.
or if the product is required for more than 10 days

items.t: Elderly: higher risk of serious adverse effects; lowest effective dose for the shortest time; monitor regularly for GI bleeding.

src.q: The elderly are at increased risk of serious consequences of adverse reactions.
The patient should be monitored regularly for GI bleeding during NSAID therapy.

items.t: MHRA: avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2400 mg/day or more) in established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease, congestive heart failure (NYHA II-III) or uncontrolled hypertension. No increased cardiovascular risk seen up to 1200 mg/day.

src.q: avoid use of high-dose ibuprofen (≥2400 mg per day) in patients with established: ischaemic heart disease peripheral arterial disease cerebrovascular disease congestive heart failure
consider that no increase in cardiovascular risk is seen with ibuprofen at doses up to 1200 mg per day

items.t: Tablets, children: 20 mg/kg/day in divided doses; juvenile rheumatoid arthritis up to 40 mg/kg/day in divided doses. Not recommended under 7 kg; more suitable formulations exist for young children.

src.q: Children: The daily dosage of Brufen is 20 mg/kg of body weight in divided doses. For young children, more suitable formulations are available.
In Juvenile Rheumatoid Arthritis, up to 40 mg/kg of body weight daily in divided doses may be taken. Not recommended for children weighing less than 7 kg.

items.t: Suspension, pain and fever: 20 mg/kg/day in divided doses. By age: 3-6 months (over 5 kg) 2.5 ml up to 3 times in 24 hours, no longer than 24 hours; 6 months-1 year 2.5 ml 3-4 times a day; 1-4 years 5 ml three times a day; 4-7 years 7.5 ml three times a day; 7-12 years 10 ml three times a day.

src.q: For pain and fever - 20 mg/kg/day in divided doses (including OTC use).
Infants 3-6 months weighing more than 5 kg: One 2.5 ml dose may be taken 3 times in 24 hours. Do not use for more than 24 hours
Infants 6 months-1 year: 2.5 ml three to four times a day. Children 1-4 years: 5 ml three times a day. Children 4-7 years: 7.5 ml three times a day. Children 7-12 years: 10 ml three times a day.

items.t: Post-immunisation fever: 2.5 ml (50 mg), then one more 2.5 ml six hours later if needed; no more than 2 doses in 24 hours.

src.q: Post-immunisation fever: 2.5 ml (50 mg) followed by one further dose of 2.5 ml (50 mg) six hours later if necessary. No more than 2 doses in 24 hours.

items.t: Juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (prescription only, suspension): up to 30-40 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 divided doses.

src.q: For Juvenile Rheumatoid Arthritis (prescription only use): Doses up to 30-40mg/kg/day may be taken in three or four divided doses.

items.t: Do not give under 3 months. Infants 3-5 months: seek advice if symptoms worsen or persist beyond 24 hours; from 6 months seek advice if needed for more than 3 days.

src.q: Do not give to children under 3 months of age.
If in children aged from 6 months and in adolescents this medicinal product is required for more than 3 days, or if symptoms worsen a doctor should be consulted.

items.t: Risk of renal impairment in dehydrated children and adolescents.

src.q: There is a risk of renal impairment in dehydrated children and adolescents.

src.q: Patients who have previously shown hypersensitivity reactions (e.g. asthma, rhinitis, angioedema or urticaria) after taking ibuprofen, aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).

src.q: History of gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation, related to previous NSAID therapy. items.t: GI bleeding, ulceration or perforation can occur at any time and can be fatal; risk rises with dose, ulcer history and age. Start at the lowest dose; consider misoprostol or a PPI in these patients and with low-dose aspirin or other drugs raising GI risk. Stop if GI bleeding or ulceration occurs.

src.q: Combination therapy with protective agents (e.g. misoprostol or proton pump inhibitors) should be considered for these patients
When GI bleeding or ulceration occurs in patients receiving Brufen, the treatment should be withdrawn.

items.t: Cardiovascular: high dose (2400 mg/day) may slightly increase arterial thrombotic risk; low dose (1200 mg/day or less) not shown to. Uncontrolled hypertension, heart failure NYHA II-III, ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease: only after careful consideration and avoid 2400 mg/day.

src.q: Patients with uncontrolled hypertension, congestive heart failure (NYHA II-III), established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, and/or cerebrovascular disease should only be treated with ibuprofen after careful consideration and high doses (2400mg/day) should be avoided.

items.t: Renal: may precipitate renal failure; highest risk with renal, cardiac or liver impairment, diuretics, ACE inhibitors and in the elderly. Use lowest dose, shortest time and monitor renal function. Caution in significant dehydration.

src.q: For these patients, use the lowest effective dose, for the shortest possible duration and monitor renal function especially in long-term treated patients
Caution should be used when initiating treatment with ibuprofen in patients with considerable dehydration.

items.t: Asthma, chronic rhinitis or allergic disease: caution (bronchospasm, urticaria, angioedema).

src.q: Caution is required if Brufen is administered to patients suffering from, or with a previous history of, bronchial asthma, chronic rhinitis or allergic diseases

items.t: Ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease: give with care (may be exacerbated). SLE / mixed connective tissue disease: increased risk of aseptic meningitis.

src.q: NSAIDs should be given with care to patients with a history of ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease as these conditions may be exacerbated
In patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and mixed connective tissue disorders there may be an increased risk of aseptic meningitis

items.t: Severe skin reactions (SJS, TEN, DRESS, AGEP): stop immediately at first signs. Avoid in chickenpox. May mask signs of infection.

src.q: If signs and symptoms suggestive of these reactions appear ibuprofen should be withdrawn immediately
Thus, it is advisable to avoid use of Ibuprofen in case of varicella.

items.t: Avoid with other NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors.

src.q: The use of Brufen with concomitant NSAIDs, including cyclooxygenase-2 selective inhibitors, should be avoided due to the increased risk of ulceration or bleeding

items.t: Renal tubular acidosis and hypokalaemia with long-term high doses (usually over 4 weeks) or overdose.

src.q: Renal tubular acidosis and hypokalaemia may occur following acute overdose and in patients taking ibuprofen products over long periods at high doses (typically greater than 4 weeks)

items.t: Anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin): NSAIDs may enhance their effect. Antiplatelets and SSRIs: increased GI bleeding risk. Corticosteroids: increased GI ulceration or bleeding.

src.q: Anticoagulants: NSAIDs may enhance the effects of anticoagulants, such as warfarin
Anti-platelet agents and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs): Increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding with NSAIDs
Corticosteroids: Increased risk of gastrointestinal ulceration or bleeding with NSAIDs

items.t: ACE inhibitors, angiotensin-II receptor antagonists, beta-blockers, diuretics: reduced antihypertensive effect; diuretics increase nephrotoxicity risk.

src.q: NSAIDs may reduce the effect of anti-hypertensives, such as ACE inhibitors, angiotensin-II receptor antagonists, beta-blockers and diuretics. Diuretics can also increase the risk of nephrotoxicity of NSAIDs.

items.t: Methotrexate: NSAIDs may reduce methotrexate clearance. Tablets SmPC: take care. Suspension SmPC lists methotrexate under combinations to avoid.

src.q: Methotrexate: NSAIDs may inhibit the tubular secretion of methotrexate and reduce clearance of methotrexate.
Ibuprofen should be avoided in combination with:

items.t: Quinolone antibiotics: possible increased risk of convulsions.

src.q: Patients taking NSAIDs and quinolones may have an increased risk of developing convulsions.

items.t: Aspirin: not generally recommended together; regular ibuprofen may reduce the cardioprotective effect of low-dose aspirin. Other NSAIDs: avoid.

src.q: the possibility that regular, long-term use of ibuprofen may reduce the cardioprotective effect of low-dose acetylsalicylic acid cannot be excluded
Avoid concomitant use of two or more NSAIDs, including Cox-2 inhibitors

items.t: Others: lithium (reduced elimination), ciclosporin and tacrolimus (nephrotoxicity), sulfonylureas (hypoglycaemia, rare), CYP2C9 inhibitors such as fluconazole/voriconazole (consider ibuprofen dose reduction), zidovudine, cardiac glycosides.

src.q: Lithium: Decreased elimination of lithium.
Reduction of the ibuprofen dose should be considered when potent CYP2C9 inhibitors are administered concomitantly

src.q: may lead to severe hyperkalaemia

rules.consequence: NSAIDs may enhance anticoagulant effects; increased risk of ulceration or bleeding.
rules.action: Use with caution.

Patients at greatest risk of this reaction are those with impaired renal function, heart failure, liver dysfunction, those taking diuretics and ACE inhibitors and the elderly.

src.q: Diuretics can also increase the risk of nephrotoxicity of NSAIDs.

src.q: The following examples should be avoided, or administered with caution with increased clinical and laboratory monitoring
NSAIDs (including aspirin and cox-2 specific NSAIDS)

rules.consequence: Spironolactone SmPC: use with NSAIDs may lead to severe hyperkalaemia.
rules.action: Caution; spironolactone SmPC advises regular monitoring of fluid and electrolyte status.

src.q: Concomitant use of Aldactone with other potassium-sparing diuretics, angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
may lead to severe hyperkalaemia
Fluid and electrolyte status should be regularly monitored

rules.consequence: Lisinopril SmPC: worsening renal function, including possible acute renal failure, and a rise in serum potassium, especially with poor renal function.
rules.action: Caution, especially in the elderly; keep hydrated; consider monitoring renal function after starting and periodically (lisinopril SmPC).
rules.sourceWording: The combination should be administered with caution

src.q: Concomitant use of ACE inhibitors and NSAIDs may lead to an increased risk of worsening of renal function, including possible acute renal failure, and an increase in serum potassium
The combination should be administered with caution, especially in the elderly.

rules.consequence: Metformin SmPC: NSAIDs can impair renal function, which may increase the risk of lactic acidosis.
rules.action: Close monitoring of renal function when starting or using the combination (metformin SmPC).
rules.sourceWording: close monitoring of renal function is necessary

src.q: NSAIDs, including selective cyclo-oxygenase (COX) II inhibitors
When starting or using such products in combination with metformin, close monitoring of renal function is necessary.

rules.consequence: Increased risk of methotrexate toxicity and renal toxicity (reduced renal elimination).
rules.action: Use with caution on specialist advice (SPS); methotrexate SmPC: not recommended if any renal impairment, including mild.
rules.sourceWording: Use NSAIDs in combination with methotrexate with caution on the advice of the specialist

src.q: Taking methotrexate and NSAIDs can increase the risk of methotrexate toxicity.
Use NSAIDs in combination with methotrexate with caution on the advice of the specialist (for example, rheumatologist).
If risk factors such as renal function disorders, including mild renal impairment, are present, combined administration with NSAIDs is not recommended.
